# 1975–1985: The Architecture of Family

The decade of the 1980s is often remembered as the era when the American dream became complicated—the decade of stagflation and Reaganomics, of deindustrialization and cultural conflict. But for Bob and Nancy, raising Heather and Bobby in suburban Michigan, the 1980s were the years when family became the central project, the framework around which everything else organized itself.
